neutrality.title: A long-term family base
neutrality.subtitle: Start with the life you intend to build
neutrality.stat1Label: Choose a municipality around daily life
neutrality.p1: For a high-net-worth family, the location decision reaches beyond a tax comparison. Consider where children will study, how often you need to travel, which languages the household uses and where business responsibilities remain. A useful shortlist begins with those facts.
neutrality.p2: Turn broad preferences into a home, school and workplace combination that can be tested. Visit the municipality, try daily journeys and decide what would make a staged move preferable to moving everyone at once.

banking.title: Banking and wealth coordination
banking.subtitle: Choose services around your assets and reporting needs
banking.stat3Label: Compare fees and the proposed mandate
banking.p1: Separate the jobs you need a bank to perform. Personal wealth, an operating company and a family office may require different accounts, reporting and relationships. Ask institutions to confirm whether they can consider your residence, tax status and proposed assets.
banking.p2: Prepare the evidence of how wealth was accumulated and where expected transfers will come from. Banks make their own acceptance decisions. Relocation coordination helps sequence the preparation and introductions with the wider move; it does not guarantee an account or investment outcome.

education.title: School choice for international families
education.subtitle: Match the curriculum, language and journey to the child
education.stat3Label: Test the journey for the child’s grade
education.p1: Compare public and international education around your children’s ages, current studies, language needs and likely length of stay. Local public schooling can support integration; an international curriculum may suit a family maintaining continuity across countries. Ask the schools what support is available.
education.p2: Confirm admissions and the correct campus before choosing a home. Include travel, after-school arrangements and any learning support in the comparison. A school’s reputation does not establish availability, suitability for an individual child or future university admission.

healthcare.title: Healthcare preparation
healthcare.subtitle: Plan continuity of care as part of the move
healthcare.stat1Label: Confirm insurance duties and start dates
healthcare.p1: Swiss residence normally brings a requirement to obtain health insurance, with exceptions depending on the circumstances. Confirm the position for each family member, the deadline and the effective date through the relevant authority or insurer. Include premiums and personal cost-sharing in the household budget.
healthcare.p2: Before arrival, identify existing prescriptions, ongoing treatment and the records a new clinician will need. Ask providers about appointment availability and language needs. Coverage and clinical decisions belong with insurers and healthcare professionals.

tax.title: Personal and business tax planning
tax.subtitle: Compare complete scenarios with qualified advisers
tax.p1: Compare the same facts across shortlisted municipalities: household income, assets, family circumstances and the actual business plan. Personal residence and company location need separate analysis. Request a written calculation with assumptions and the applicable tax year rather than choosing from a headline rate.
tax.p2: Expenditure-based taxation is available to qualifying foreign nationals who become Swiss tax resident for the first time or after at least ten years abroad and do not undertake gainful activity in Switzerland. Both spouses living together must meet the conditions. Managing a business or family office from Switzerland needs specific assessment; foreign clients or ownership alone do not establish eligibility.

qualityOfLife.title: Test everyday life
qualityOfLife.subtitle: The practical details decide whether a location fits
qualityOfLife.stat1Label: Visit at the time you would travel
qualityOfLife.stat3Label: Explore the places your family would use
qualityOfLife.p1: Use a scouting visit to test the ordinary week. Look at shops, transport, activities, school routes and access to the services you rely on. Compare an apartment near work with a larger home that requires more travel.
qualityOfLife.p2: Budget using current housing enquiries, school information and insurance quotes. Keep deposits, recurring costs and one-off relocation expenses separate. The relocation budget planner lets you compare Zurich, Zug and Schwyz using your own figures.

business.title: A Swiss base for entrepreneurs
business.subtitle: Connect the operating model with the founder’s move
business.stat1Label: Define what will happen in Switzerland
business.stat2Label: Confirm the right to live and work
business.p1: A business move starts with the proposed activities: management, employees, customers, contracts, assets and financing. Ask specialists to compare suitable structures and the cross-border implications. A company can be incorporated without resolving every immigration, tax, banking or licensing question.
business.p2: Before an exit or restructuring, coordinate advisers in the departure country and Switzerland. Record intended work after the transaction, retained ownership and any deferred payments. Build the family move around assessed facts and confirmed dependencies.

services.subtitle: Relocation planning for private wealth, active businesses and international families
services.pageSubtitle: Coordinate Swiss residence, business and family priorities

assetStructuring.title: Pre-Immigration Tax & Asset Planning
assetStructuring.description: Map business ownership, investments and planned transactions before moving. Coordinate Swiss and departure-country tax advice.
assetStructuring.detail: Before establishing Swiss tax residence, map shareholdings, trusts, pensions, property, debts, planned disposals and the countries involved. Collect ownership records, valuations and source-of-wealth evidence. Ask your existing and Swiss specialists to assess departure taxes, treaty residence and the consequences of each transaction. Do not assume that selling before arrival is tax-free or that a foreign structure retains its treatment in Switzerland.
assetStructuring.seoTitle: Pre-Immigration Tax Planning for HNWIs & Founders

lumpSum.title: Lump-Sum Taxation (Forfait Fiscal)
lumpSum.description: Assess expenditure-based taxation eligibility, canton requirements and the comparison with ordinary Swiss taxation.
lumpSum.detail: Expenditure-based taxation is available to qualifying foreign nationals who become Swiss tax resident for the first time or after at least ten years abroad and do not undertake gainful activity in Switzerland. Both spouses living together must meet the conditions. Managing a business or family office from Switzerland needs specific assessment; foreign clients or ownership alone do not establish eligibility.
lumpSum.seoTitle: Swiss Lump-Sum Taxation for Eligible Private Clients

residency.title: Residency & Immigration
residency.description: Assess Swiss residence and work options for entrepreneurs, private clients and families before making relocation commitments.
residency.detail:
EU/EFTA nationals can qualify through employment, self-employment or residence without gainful activity. The latter requires sufficient resources and adequate health and accident insurance. Permit duration depends on the basis of admission. Submit the documentation requested by the local authority; processing time is not a national guarantee.

For non-EU/EFTA nationals, the legal basis must be assessed individually. Employment, self-employment, retirement and exceptional admissions have different requirements. Wealth, a property purchase, company incorporation or a tax ruling does not by itself confer a residence permit. Cantonal and, where required, federal authorities decide; obtain an assessment before committing to a move.
residency.seoTitle: Swiss Residency for Entrepreneurs & Private Clients

companyFormation.title: Company Formation & Business Relocation
companyFormation.description: Coordinate company setup, founder work permission, governance and cross-border tax questions for a Swiss business base.
companyFormation.detail:
A Swiss AG requires at least CHF 100,000 share capital; at incorporation at least 20% of each share’s nominal value and at least CHF 50,000 in total must be paid in. A GmbH requires CHF 20,000 fully paid in. Swiss-resident representation and the applicable governance, licensing and reporting duties must be arranged with qualified specialists.

Start with what the business will actually do in Switzerland: who manages it, where the team works, which customers it serves and what contracts or assets may move. Incorporating a company is separate from obtaining the founder’s right to work. Ask specialists to assess payroll, social insurance, VAT, licensing and the implications for existing overseas entities.

We coordinate the relocation workstream with your corporate and tax advisers. The engagement should specify who handles incorporation, banking, permits and ongoing administration.
companyFormation.seoTitle: Swiss Company Formation & Relocation for Entrepreneurs

familyOffice.title: Family Office Establishment
familyOffice.description: Define the Swiss office’s remit, governance and reporting needs; coordinate specialist advice, banking preparation and family relocation.
familyOffice.detail:
Begin with the family’s needs: investment oversight, consolidated reporting, administration, succession or support for an operating business. Compare an internal team, external providers and a hybrid arrangement before committing to an entity.

The ownership, clients and activities determine which regulatory questions need assessment. A family office label does not settle licensing obligations. Agree responsibility for investment decisions, custody, tax advice and reporting with the appointed professionals. We connect that work with the family’s residence, home and school plans.
familyOffice.seoTitle: Swiss Family Office Setup & UHNW Relocation

directorship.title: Directorship & Board Coordination
directorship.description: Coordinate Swiss representation, board responsibilities and administration alongside your company and relocation advisers.
directorship.detail:
A Swiss business needs a governance arrangement suited to its legal form and actual operations. Review resident representation, signing authority, board duties and record keeping with corporate counsel.

A resident representative does not by itself establish all the substance a business may need for tax, banking or licensing purposes. Agree the director’s mandate, information access, remuneration and ongoing responsibilities in writing.

realEstate.title: Real Estate Advisory
realEstate.description: Plan a Swiss home search around residence eligibility, school routes and budget, with Lex Koller and purchase questions assessed by specialists.
realEstate.detail:
Property eligibility depends on nationality, actual domicile, permit and intended use. A B permit is not blanket permission to acquire Swiss residential investments. A qualifying main-home purchase and a holiday or rental property are different cases. A Swiss company does not bypass Lex Koller if it is foreign-controlled. Ask the competent cantonal authority and notary to confirm the position before signing.

For a first move, compare renting with buying before committing to a location. Build the shortlist around the actual school campus, workplace and everyday travel. Request current property particulars and a full acquisition budget, including financing and professional costs.
realEstate.seoTitle: Swiss Property & Relocation Advisory for Private Clients

health.title: Health & Wellness Coordination
health.description: Coordinate health insurance preparation and healthcare introductions around your family’s medical and relocation needs.
health.detail:
Include healthcare in the move plan before arrival. Identify ongoing treatment, prescriptions, language needs and the records your next clinician will require. Confirm insurance obligations and start dates for each family member, including any applicable exception.

We help coordinate practical arrangements and introductions. Insurers and healthcare providers confirm coverage, acceptance, availability and costs; medical decisions remain with your clinicians.
health.seoTitle: Swiss Health Insurance & Healthcare Relocation Support

lifestyle.title: Family Settlement & School Coordination
lifestyle.description: Coordinate school enquiries, housing, local orientation and family settlement, with admissions and permit decisions confirmed by the relevant institutions.
lifestyle.detail:
Start with your children’s ages, language needs and education plans, then compare public and international school options. Check places and the journey to the correct campus before committing to a home. Admissions decisions remain with the school.

Build a practical arrival plan for insurance, registration, daily transport and community connections. If domestic staff may move with you, assess their immigration and employment position separately before making commitments.

swiss-lump-sum-taxation-guide.title: Swiss Lump-Sum Taxation for HNWIs: Eligibility and Planning
swiss-lump-sum-taxation-guide.metaDescription: Assess Swiss lump-sum taxation eligibility, the 2026 assessment base, canton choice and the implications of continued business activity after a move.
swiss-lump-sum-taxation-guide.excerpt: Assess Swiss lump-sum taxation eligibility, the 2026 assessment base, canton choice and the implications of continued business activity after a move.

0.heading: Eligibility Requirements
0.content: Expenditure-based taxation is available to qualifying foreign nationals who become Swiss tax resident for the first time or after at least ten years abroad and do not undertake gainful activity in Switzerland. Both spouses living together must meet the conditions. Managing a business or family office from Switzerland needs specific assessment; foreign clients or ownership alone do not establish eligibility.

1.heading: How the Taxable Base Is Calculated
1.content: For tax year 2026, the federal minimum assessment base is CHF 435,000, not the tax payable. Worldwide living expenses and statutory housing-based minimums must also be considered. A separate control calculation can increase the tax due on specified Swiss income and treaty-relieved foreign income. Cantonal income and wealth-tax rules require a separate calculation.

2.heading: Which cantons should you compare?
2.content: Zürich abolished cantonal expenditure-based taxation in 2010. Schaffhausen, Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Basel-Landschaft and Basel-Stadt also abolished it. For other cantons, obtain the current requirements from the relevant tax authority. A single national table of minimum payments cannot establish your eligibility or final liability.

3.heading: The Application Process: Step by Step
3.content: Before choosing a canton, assemble passports, residence history, a worldwide household budget, housing details, income sources and intended work activities. Coordinate a comparison with ordinary taxation and, where appropriate, a written ruling request through qualified tax specialists. Confirm its assumptions and reporting duties. Tax treatment and immigration permission are separate decisions; neither approval nor a fixed annual tax bill is guaranteed.

4.heading: Founders: describe your role after the move
4.content:
If you are preparing a business exit, distinguish ownership from the work you will continue to perform. List board positions, consulting agreements, management duties and any earn-out conditions. Ask your tax and immigration advisers to assess the proposed activities together before relying on a private-wealth residence plan.

The location of customers or the company’s registered office does not, on its own, settle how work performed from Switzerland will be treated.

5.heading: Questions for the first assessment
5.content:
Bring a broad summary of citizenship, residence history, family members, intended activities and the countries connected to your assets. Compare the household’s expected spending, housing and specialist costs alongside the tax analysis.

A useful outcome is a written list of assumptions, unresolved questions and the next authority or adviser decision. Keep transaction deadlines separate from proposed relocation dates until the dependencies are understood.

lex-koller-swiss-real-estate.title: Buying Swiss Property as a Foreigner: Lex Koller and Relocation
lex-koller-swiss-real-estate.metaDescription: Plan a Swiss home purchase around nationality, residence status, property use and Lex Koller. Practical questions for HNW families and entrepreneurs.
lex-koller-swiss-real-estate.excerpt: Plan a Swiss home purchase around nationality, residence status, property use and Lex Koller. Practical questions for HNW families and entrepreneurs.

0.heading: Start with the buyer and intended use
0.content: Property eligibility depends on nationality, actual domicile, permit and intended use. A B permit is not blanket permission to acquire Swiss residential investments. A qualifying main-home purchase and a holiday or rental property are different cases. A Swiss company does not bypass Lex Koller if it is foreign-controlled. Ask the competent cantonal authority and notary to confirm the position before signing.

1.heading: Residence permission is a separate decision
1.content:
Owning Swiss property does not give a foreign national a right to a residence permit. Establish the proposed residence basis before treating a home purchase as part of a confirmed move.

For a family using several international homes, explain which property will actually be the main home and how it will be used. Ask the competent authority and notary to assess the specific transaction, including any ownership through a company or other structure.

2.heading: Build a full acquisition brief
2.content:
Record the proposed buyers, financing, intended occupancy and whether any part will be rented out. Ask the notary which confirmations are needed before signing and which contractual conditions are appropriate.

Request current property particulars and a full cost estimate. Compare financing, transaction costs, maintenance and any renovation needs. A canton-wide price per square metre is a poor substitute for a specific property assessment.

3.heading: For entrepreneurs: protect the wider timetable
3.content:
If the purchase depends on business-sale proceeds or a new banking relationship, align the payment schedule with confirmed funds and professional advice. Do not assume a bank will open an account or provide financing by a seller’s deadline.

Check whether renting first would allow the family to test a school route and neighbourhood while the longer-term residence and purchase questions are resolved.

4.heading: Confirm the rules at the point of commitment
4.content:
The cantonal authority responsible for the property decides questions about authorisation. The Federal Office of Justice publishes the framework and contacts; proposed legal revisions should not be confused with rules already in force.

Ask your notary or legal adviser to check the current position for your facts before committing. Our role is to coordinate the home search with the family’s permit, school and arrival plan.

best-international-schools-zurich-zug-sc.title: International Schools near Zurich, Zug and Schwyz: A Family Guide
best-international-schools-zurich-zug-sc.metaDescription: Compare school locations near Zurich, Zug and Schwyz. Plan campus visits, admissions questions, fees and the school commute using direct school sources.
best-international-schools-zurich-zug-sc.excerpt: Check the right campus, ask better admissions questions and compare the full cost and daily journey before choosing a home.

0.content: School choice and housing should be planned together. This guide introduces international and bilingual options in the Zurich and Zug area for families considering homes in Zurich, Zug or Schwyz. It is a starting shortlist, not a ranking: the right fit depends on your child’s age, language, learning needs and likely next move. The schools named here are in Zurich or Zug; a home in Schwyz requires checking the actual cross-canton commute.

1.heading: International Schools in Zurich
1.content: Begin with the exact campus for your child’s age, rather than the school’s name alone. A home that works for a primary campus may create a different journey when a child moves to secondary school. Include both journeys if siblings would attend different campuses.

2.heading: Zurich International School (ZIS)
2.content: ZIS has two campuses: Wädenswil for ages 3–11 and Adliswil for ages 11–18. Confirm the campus and programme for your child’s year group directly with the school before choosing a home. Request the current fee schedule and a written decision on availability; a relocation adviser cannot guarantee a place.

3.heading: Inter-Community School Zurich (ICS)
3.content: Inter-Community School Zurich is based in Zumikon and offers the IB continuum. Ask admissions about the appropriate year group, language support and any learning support your child needs. Request the current fee schedule directly from the school, including application charges and services outside tuition. Compare the journey from your shortlisted home during school travel hours.

4.heading: Swiss International School (SIS) Zurich
4.content: SIS Zürich-Wollishofen offers bilingual German-English kindergarten and primary school. For an older child, check the relevant SIS location, qualifications and admission requirements directly with the school. Do not assume that every campus offers every stage of the wider SIS network.

5.heading: International Schools in Zug
5.content: For families considering Zug or nearby Schwyz, compare school location with both parents’ work journeys and the child’s weekly activities. A canton-wide comparison is too broad: record the home address, campus and transport option for each candidate.

6.heading: International School of Zug and Luzern (ISZL)
6.content: ISZL’s Zug Campus is in Baar and serves Early Years through Grade 8. Its Riverside Campus is in Hünenberg and serves Grades 9–12; Riverside is not in Lucerne. Applications are accepted throughout the year, subject to availability. Ask admissions which campus, programme and support arrangements fit your child.

7.heading: Institut Montana Zugerberg
7.content: Institut Montana on the Zugerberg offers day and boarding education, with international and Swiss educational pathways. Confirm the programme, language requirements and qualification suited to your child. Request separate quotations for day and boarding arrangements, and ask what supervision, meals, travel and weekend arrangements are included. A boarding option should be assessed against your child’s needs rather than treated as a solution to a long commute.

8.heading: Curriculum Comparison: IB vs. Swiss Matura vs. American/British
8.content: Work backwards from the child’s likely next school or university destination. Ask which qualifications the chosen programme awards and check the receiving institution’s subject, language and admission requirements directly. Do not assume that an international curriculum, an IB Diploma or a Swiss Matura removes every admission condition. For a child already partway through an examination programme, discuss subject continuity and transfer timing before changing schools.

9.heading: Admissions Timeline and Practical Advice
9.content: Start with your child’s current year group, languages, learning support needs and intended start date. Ask each school for written confirmation of availability, required documents and the full fee schedule, including transport, meals and other extras. Arrange a visit or online meeting and test the school-day journey from candidate homes. Admission decisions belong to the school; we cannot guarantee a place or priority admission.

relocating-to-switzerland-timeline.title: Swiss Relocation Timeline for Entrepreneurs and HNW Families
relocating-to-switzerland-timeline.metaDescription: Sequence a Swiss move around residence eligibility, business decisions, banking, schools and housing. Plan dependencies without relying on fixed approval dates.
relocating-to-switzerland-timeline.excerpt: Sequence a Swiss move around residence eligibility, business decisions, banking, schools and housing. Plan dependencies without relying on fixed approval dates.

0.heading: Plan around decisions, not a promised moving date
0.content:
The timeline for a Swiss move depends on the proposed residence basis, document readiness, family needs and the decisions of authorities and institutions. An entrepreneur launching operations may face different dependencies from a family living on private wealth.

Start with a target window and identify which commitments are flexible. Treat a business sale, school start, expiring lease or medical need as a planning constraint rather than evidence that an approval can be accelerated.

1.heading: First: establish the residence and work basis
1.content:
Record citizenship, current residence status, family relationships and each adult’s planned work. Review the relevant route with an immigration specialist before signing a long lease or relying on a Swiss company to support the move.

For founders, describe the business activity, financing, management role and proposed Swiss operations. For private clients, establish whether the intended activities are consistent with the residence and tax arrangements being assessed.

2.heading: Before transactions: align advisers in both countries
2.content:
Build a list of shareholdings, investments, property, pensions, trusts and planned disposals. Ask departure-country and Swiss advisers to review residence dates, transaction timing and reporting responsibilities together.

A pre-exit founder should include the expected sale process, any continued employment or board role and deferred payments. The relocation timetable should follow that analysis; do not assume that moving before a sale determines its tax treatment.

3.heading: In parallel: test the canton and family shortlist
3.content:
Compare actual municipalities, homes and school campuses. Check admissions requirements and available places directly with schools. Use a trial journey between the proposed home, workplace and campus when you can.

Prepare a household budget including temporary accommodation, rent, deposits, insurance and professional costs. Keep a fallback for housing or a delayed school place, rather than treating every workstream as certain to finish together.

4.heading: Prepare applications and banking evidence
4.content:
Agree the authority’s document list, translations or certification needs and submission responsibilities. Banking preparation can run alongside this work, but a bank has its own acceptance process. Keep the evidence of business ownership and expected funds consistent with the wider plan.

Maintain one decision log: owner, documents outstanding, next response and commitment affected. This makes it easier to adjust the move date when a dependency changes.

5.heading: Arrival and the first month
5.content:
Check the registration and work-start requirements for your particular permit route before travelling. Confirm local registration, insurance arrangements, school start dates, utility handover and the practicalities of receiving official correspondence.

Once settled, schedule the handover to ongoing tax, accounting and other advisers. Keep permit renewals and reporting dates in a shared calendar. Our relocation checklist, first-30-days guide and budget planner help organise the practical tasks; they do not predict approval dates.

opening-swiss-private-bank-account.title: Swiss Private Banking for HNWIs and Entrepreneurs
opening-swiss-private-bank-account.metaDescription: Prepare for Swiss private banking: source of wealth, business-sale proceeds, ownership records, fees and the bank’s independent acceptance decision.
opening-swiss-private-bank-account.excerpt: Prepare for Swiss private banking: source of wealth, business-sale proceeds, ownership records, fees and the bank’s independent acceptance decision.

0.heading: Start with the banking job to be done
0.content:
Before approaching a Swiss private bank, write down what you need: everyday payments, custody, investment advice, discretionary management or support for a family office. A founder may also need a separate operating account for a business. Distinguish personal, corporate and family-structure requirements so each application has a clear purpose.

Your residence, citizenship, tax status, assets and intended transactions affect which institutions can consider the relationship. Ask the bank to confirm its current client criteria before investing time in a full application.

1.heading: Source of wealth and source of funds
1.content:
Swiss financial institutions must identify clients and beneficial owners and assess relevant money-laundering risks. For preparation, distinguish how the overall wealth was accumulated from where the particular transfer will come from.

A business owner’s file might connect company ownership, accounts, dividends or a sale agreement to the receiving account. An inheritance may call for estate documents; investment proceeds may need a traceable holding and transaction history. These are preparation examples. The bank sets the evidence requirements for the actual case.

2.heading: Before and after a business sale
2.content:
Coordinate banking preparation with the transaction timetable. Explain the seller, buyer, consideration, expected payment dates and any deferred proceeds or retained ownership. Ask your lawyers and tax advisers which records can be shared and through which secure channel.

Do not move a completion date or route proceeds through a new entity simply to fit an assumed banking timetable. Confirm the receiving account is ready and that the bank understands the expected transfer before completion.

3.heading: Digital assets and complex ownership
3.content:
For digital-asset wealth, organise exchange statements, wallet histories and evidence connecting the assets to their owner. Explain significant gaps to the bank before making transfer plans. Acceptance of a particular token, platform, transaction history or structure is a bank-specific decision.

For holding companies, trusts and foundations, prepare a clear ownership and control map. More layers can mean more questions. A polished narrative does not replace the records the bank needs to assess the relationship.

4.heading: Compare fees, service and decision authority
4.content:
Request a written proposal covering minimum relationship size, custody and advisory fees, transaction charges, foreign exchange, reporting and any exit costs. Published figures may not apply to your residence, mandate or asset mix.

Ask who will service the account, what can be done online and how the institution works with your existing advisers. Review investment risks and mandate terms with the appropriate professionals; relocating does not require placing all assets with one provider.

5.heading: What relocation coordination can help with
5.content:
We help place banking preparation in the wider move plan and coordinate introductions where suitable. The institution makes its own acceptance decision and may request further information or decline the relationship. There is no universal account-opening deadline.

Use the initial enquiry to explain your priorities and broad circumstances. Send passports, statements and transaction documents only through the secure channel agreed with the relevant professional or bank.

swiss-residency-permits-guide.title: Swiss Residence Permits for Entrepreneurs and HNW Families
swiss-residency-permits-guide.metaDescription: Understand Swiss residence planning for entrepreneurs and high-net-worth families: EU/EFTA and third-country routes, work, family inclusion and settlement.
swiss-residency-permits-guide.excerpt: Understand Swiss residence planning for entrepreneurs and high-net-worth families: EU/EFTA and third-country routes, work, family inclusion and settlement.

0.heading: Residence planning
0.content: Understanding Switzerland's residency permit system is fundamental to any relocation plan. The type of permit you hold affects everything — from your tax treatment and property rights to your family's stability and long-term options. This guide covers the main permit categories, their requirements, and the pathway from initial residence to Swiss citizenship.

1.heading: Overview of the Swiss Permit System
1.content: B is a residence permit, L a short-stay permit, C a settlement permit and G a cross-border commuter permit. The appropriate category and its conditions depend on nationality, purpose of stay and the authority’s decision.

2.heading: The B Permit: Your Gateway to Switzerland
2.content: The B permit is the standard residence permit for foreign nationals living in Switzerland. However, the application process and conditions differ significantly based on nationality.

3.heading: EU/EFTA Nationals
3.content: EU/EFTA nationals can qualify through employment, self-employment or residence without gainful activity. The latter requires sufficient resources and adequate health and accident insurance. Permit duration depends on the basis of admission. Submit the documentation requested by the local authority; processing time is not a national guarantee.

4.heading: Non-EU/EFTA Nationals
4.content: For non-EU/EFTA nationals, the legal basis must be assessed individually. Employment, self-employment, retirement and exceptional admissions have different requirements. Wealth, a property purchase, company incorporation or a tax ruling does not by itself confer a residence permit. Cantonal and, where required, federal authorities decide; obtain an assessment before committing to a move.

5.heading: The C Permit: Permanent Settlement
5.content: A C settlement permit may be granted after five or ten years depending on nationality, applicable agreements, residence history and integration. Five years is not a universal EU rule. Settlement and later citizenship are separate applications, subject to their own conditions; neither follows automatically from a B permit.

6.heading: Family Inclusion
6.content: Family rules depend on the sponsor’s nationality and permit. Under EU/EFTA free movement, qualifying family can include a spouse, children under 21 or dependent children, and dependent parents, subject to conditions. Third-country rules differ and can include age limits, application deadlines, housing, language and financial requirements. Check each family member before fixing school or moving dates.

7.heading: The Path to Swiss Citizenship
7.content: Ordinary naturalisation generally requires a C permit and ten years of qualifying residence, including three of the preceding five years. Years between ages 8 and 18 count double, with at least six years of actual residence. Cantonal and communal residence rules also apply, alongside language and integration requirements. Eligibility is not a promise of citizenship.

8.heading: Entrepreneurs: company ownership and the right to work
8.content:
Before forming a company for your move, describe what you will do in Switzerland and which immigration basis applies. EU/EFTA self-employment and admission of third-country entrepreneurs require different assessments.

For a third-country founder, prepare to discuss business viability, financing, qualifications and the proposed contribution to the Swiss economy with the relevant specialists and authority. Incorporation alone does not decide the application.

9.heading: High-net-worth families: assess each person’s activities
9.content:
Wealth is part of the financial picture, not a substitute for a legal residence basis. List the intended work and family role of each applicant, including a spouse who may continue a business remotely.

Keep the residence assessment separate from any tax-ruling request. Agree the sequence before a property commitment, school start or business transaction makes the move date difficult to change.

why-wealthy-families-leaving-uae-for-swi.title: Moving from the UAE to Switzerland: HNWI and Entrepreneur Planning
why-wealthy-families-leaving-uae-for-swi.metaDescription: For UAE-based founders and high-net-worth families: compare Swiss residence, business activities, tax advice, banking evidence, schools and the move sequence.
why-wealthy-families-leaving-uae-for-swi.excerpt: For UAE-based founders and high-net-worth families: compare Swiss residence, business activities, tax advice, banking evidence, schools and the move sequence.

0.heading: Define what the move needs to achieve
0.content:
For a family based in Dubai or Abu Dhabi, a Swiss move may be about education, proximity to European business interests or a longer-term family base. Write down your own reasons rather than relying on claims about where other wealthy families are moving.

Decide whether the plan is a full family move, a staged transition or an exploratory stay. These have different practical implications and should not be treated as interchangeable residence or tax arrangements.

1.heading: Your passport matters as well as your current address
1.content:
Living in the UAE does not determine which Swiss immigration rules apply. Start with each family member’s citizenship and existing status. EU/EFTA and third-country routes have different requirements.

An active entrepreneur must assess the proposed work as well as residence. A property purchase, company registration or banking relationship does not itself secure permission to live and work in Switzerland.

2.heading: Separate active entrepreneurship from private-wealth residence
2.content:
Describe what you will do after moving: manage an overseas business, serve on a board, start a Swiss company or oversee private investments. Ask specialists to assess those activities before choosing a tax route.

Expenditure-based taxation is restricted to eligible foreign nationals without gainful activity in Switzerland. It is not a general entrepreneur tax regime. Compare the relevant alternative with ordinary taxation and the family’s actual business and lifestyle plans.

3.heading: Map the business and departure questions
3.content:
Prepare an ownership chart showing UAE and other entities, where people work and where management decisions are made. Ask advisers in both countries about the implications of the proposed changes, including payroll, company management, contracts and any planned disposal.

Build a departure checklist for your specific UAE residence arrangements, dependants, housing, business responsibilities and accounts. Obtain current requirements from the relevant authority or provider before cancelling arrangements the family still needs.

4.heading: Prepare banking evidence before expected transfers
4.content:
Organise ownership records and evidence of how wealth was accumulated, alongside the origin of the funds you expect to transfer. For a business sale, connect the transaction documents and payment schedule to the receiving account.

A Swiss bank assesses the proposed relationship independently. Ask about its current client criteria, fees and evidence requirements; an introduction is not an acceptance decision.

5.heading: Compare a real school and home combination
5.content:
Choose school options using the children’s ages, current curriculum, language needs and likely length of stay. Compare public and international education, admissions and the journey to the actual campus.

Zurich, Zug and Schwyz provide different starting points for a German-speaking base. Vaud and Geneva deserve a separate comparison if French-speaking schooling or business connections are important. Test daily travel and use current housing enquiries rather than an assumed canton-wide price.

6.heading: Build a sequence the family can follow
6.content:
Agree who coordinates immigration, tax advice, banking, the home search and school enquiries. Keep a target move window with fallback arrangements for decisions outside your control.

We have helped hundreds of people move to Switzerland since 2012. Start with an online conversation about your family and business priorities; in-person meetings are available in Zurich. No sensitive financial documents are needed in the initial enquiry.

setting-up-family-office-switzerland.title: Setting Up a Swiss Family Office: Governance, Scope and Relocation
setting-up-family-office-switzerland.metaDescription: A planning guide for UHNW families considering a Swiss family office: operating model, governance, regulatory assessment and coordination with the family move.
setting-up-family-office-switzerland.excerpt: A planning guide for UHNW families considering a Swiss family office: operating model, governance, regulatory assessment and coordination with the family move.

0.heading: Define the purpose before choosing the structure
0.content:
A Swiss family office can be considered alongside a family’s move, a business sale or a change in generational responsibility. Start by listing the jobs it must perform: consolidated reporting, investment oversight, payments, administration, philanthropy or coordination of external advisers.

Separate the family’s personal affairs from the operating business. Record which assets, entities, countries and family members fall within scope, and which decisions remain with existing teams.

1.heading: Internal team, external providers or a hybrid model
1.content:
Compare an internal team with outsourcing particular functions and combining the two. The useful question is whether the model matches the complexity, service expectations and time the family wants to commit. A single assets-under-management threshold cannot answer that.

Request proposals against the same brief. Compare staffing, systems, custody, reporting, specialist advice and transition work. Show one-off setup expenses separately from recurring operating costs, and identify who supervises each provider.

2.heading: Regulatory assessment comes before launch
2.content:
FINMA requires authorisation for portfolio managers and trustees carrying out regulated professional activities. The assessment depends on what the office does, for whom it acts and its ownership and control arrangements.

Ask Swiss regulatory counsel to document the applicable rules and any exclusion before services begin. Do not assume that calling an entity a single family office removes regulatory obligations. Reassess if it adds unrelated clients, changes control or expands its activities.

3.heading: Company form and governance
3.content:
Where a Swiss company is appropriate, assess the legal form with corporate counsel. A Swiss AG requires at least CHF 100,000 share capital; at incorporation at least 20% of each share’s nominal value and at least CHF 50,000 in total must be paid in. A GmbH requires CHF 20,000 fully paid in. Swiss-resident representation and the applicable governance, licensing and reporting duties must be arranged with qualified specialists.

Set decision rights, signing limits, escalation procedures and access to records. Agree how investment decisions, custody, administration and independent oversight will be separated. Meeting frequency and reporting should fit the mandate and applicable requirements.

4.heading: Choose the location around real operations
4.content:
Compare the proposed workplace, recruitment needs, advisers and the family’s home location. Zurich, Zug, Schwyz, Geneva and other cantons may answer different needs; the office address and family residence need separate analysis.

Map where management decisions and work will actually take place. Ask tax specialists to assess the proposed facts across all relevant jurisdictions before treating a particular domicile as a tax solution.

5.heading: Connect the office with the family move
5.content:
The office’s formation does not give family members a Swiss residence or work entitlement. Review each person’s intended activities, especially where expenditure-based taxation is being considered. Active management from Switzerland needs assessment.

Prepare a responsibility map for corporate counsel, immigration and tax specialists, banks and the relocation coordinator. We connect that specialist work with housing, schools and arrival planning, under an agreed scope.

items.question: How long does it take to relocate to Switzerland?
items.answer: Timing depends on the residence and work basis, document readiness, authority decisions and practical arrangements such as school places and housing. Agree a target window and a sequence of decisions with your advisers; there is no single approval or settlement timeline for every Swiss move.

items.question: What is lump-sum taxation (forfait fiscal) in Switzerland?
items.answer: Expenditure-based taxation is available to qualifying foreign nationals who become Swiss tax resident for the first time or after at least ten years abroad and do not undertake gainful activity in Switzerland. Both spouses living together must meet the conditions. Managing a business or family office from Switzerland needs specific assessment; foreign clients or ownership alone do not establish eligibility. For tax year 2026, the federal minimum assessment base is CHF 435,000, not the tax payable. Worldwide living expenses and statutory housing-based minimums must also be considered. A separate control calculation can increase the tax due on specified Swiss income and treaty-relieved foreign income. Cantonal income and wealth-tax rules require a separate calculation.

items.question: Can foreigners buy property in Switzerland?
items.answer: Property eligibility depends on nationality, actual domicile, permit and intended use. A B permit is not blanket permission to acquire Swiss residential investments. A qualifying main-home purchase and a holiday or rental property are different cases. A Swiss company does not bypass Lex Koller if it is foreign-controlled. Ask the competent cantonal authority and notary to confirm the position before signing.

items.question: Which Swiss canton is best for relocation?
items.answer: Compare the actual municipality, home, school and workplace. Zurich, Zug and Schwyz suit different priorities, and the household tax comparison needs consistent assumptions about income, assets and family circumstances. Assess the company’s location separately from personal residence.

items.question: How do I open a Swiss private bank account?
items.answer: Start by clarifying the services you need and whether the bank can consider your residence, tax status and assets. Prepare identity, ownership and source-of-wealth evidence, plus records showing where expected transfers will come from. The bank decides acceptance, documentation requirements, fees and timing.

items.question: What residency permits are available in Switzerland?
items.answer: B is a residence permit, L a short-stay permit, C a settlement permit and G a cross-border commuter permit. The appropriate category and its conditions depend on nationality, purpose of stay and the authority’s decision. For non-EU/EFTA nationals, the legal basis must be assessed individually. Employment, self-employment, retirement and exceptional admissions have different requirements. Wealth, a property purchase, company incorporation or a tax ruling does not by itself confer a residence permit. Cantonal and, where required, federal authorities decide; obtain an assessment before committing to a move.

items.question: Can I move to Switzerland as an entrepreneur?
items.answer: The route depends on citizenship, existing status and proposed work. EU/EFTA self-employment and third-country entrepreneur admission have different requirements. Assess the business plan and the founder’s right to work with an immigration specialist; owning or registering a company does not itself grant a residence permit.

items.question: Do you help high-net-worth individuals and family offices?
items.answer: Yes. We coordinate relocation planning for high-net-worth individuals, entrepreneurs, UHNW families and family offices. The scope can connect residence, specialist tax questions, banking preparation, housing and schools, while your appointed professionals retain responsibility for their advice and regulated services.

faqs.question: Does moving the founder also move the company?
faqs.answer: The founder’s personal relocation and the company’s legal and tax position are separate questions. Map where management, employees, contracts and assets will sit. Ask advisers in both countries to assess the proposed facts before treating a change of home address as a company migration.

faqs.question: Should I form a Swiss company or open a branch?
faqs.answer: Compare the business purpose, ownership, liabilities, financing and planned operations with corporate and tax advisers. The suitable legal form depends on those facts. Keep the founder’s residence and work permission, bank acceptance and any sector licensing in the same project plan as separate decisions.

faqs.question: What if I am planning a business exit?
faqs.answer: Bring the proposed sale timetable, ownership chart, continued work obligations and any deferred consideration into the assessment. Coordinate your departure-country and Swiss advisers before fixing transaction and residence dates. Do not assume that a sale is tax-free because it occurs before or after the move.

faqs.question: Can I get Swiss residence by starting a company?
faqs.answer: Company registration does not itself confer residence or work permission. The assessment depends on citizenship, existing status and the proposed activity. EU/EFTA founders and third-country nationals follow different rules; establish the intended immigration basis before relying on incorporation as part of the move.

faqs.question: What should an entrepreneur prepare for the first assessment?
faqs.answer: Prepare a summary of your experience, business model, ownership, funding, expected customers and proposed Swiss team. Explain your own role and where work and management decisions will take place. A specialist can then identify which evidence and authority requirements apply to the route.

faqs.question: Can I keep managing an overseas company from Switzerland?
faqs.answer: Describe the work you intend to perform from Switzerland, even if customers and the company remain abroad. Ask immigration and tax specialists to assess that activity, including any company-management, payroll or reporting consequences. Foreign ownership or overseas clients alone do not establish a compatible residence and tax arrangement.

faqs.question: Is lump-sum taxation suitable for an active founder?
faqs.answer: Eligibility requires, among other conditions, no gainful activity in Switzerland. Describe management, board and consulting roles and assess them with qualified specialists. The regime is not a general substitute for ordinary taxation for entrepreneurs who continue working from Switzerland.

faqs.question: Is the minimum assessment base my annual tax bill?
faqs.answer: No. An assessment base is an input to the calculation, not the amount payable. Household expenditure, statutory minimums, the control calculation and cantonal rules must be considered. Compare a written scenario with ordinary taxation using the same underlying facts.

faqs.question: Does a tax ruling secure a residence permit?
faqs.answer: No. Tax treatment and permission to reside are separate decisions. Confirm the immigration basis for each family member and coordinate the applications, housing assumptions and move sequence with the appointed specialists.
